# hardware/ — case, wiring, power

[← Main README](../README.md) · Firmware pins: [firmware/](../firmware/README.md)

The physical pendant: a **round heart-shaped, two-part 3D-printed case** (≈ 48.5 × 51 × 16 mm, +1.6 mm relief) around the XIAO ESP32-S3 Sense and its LiPo, with a **raised pulse-wave relief** across the front — the vibe, the music, the heartbeat of the night. It hangs from a chain through an integrated bail loop at the top cleft. Geometry only at this stage — no texture or color.

## Design (generated by [`3dprint/pendant.py`](3dprint/pendant.py))

- **`encore_body.stl`** — back shell (16 mm deep): round-heart cavity (implicit heart curve — full lobes, bulging flanks, soft tip), **USB-C slot in the right lobe wall** (charge/flash without opening), **integrated bail ring** bridging the top cleft (chain hole front-to-back, Ø4.6), a **rim rebate** the lid drops into, and a thumb notch at the tip to pry it out.
- **`encore_lid.stl`** — front lid: a **drop-in plate** seated in the rim rebate, with the **pulse wave raised 1.6 mm** on the face (prints flat, relief up, zero supports), crush-rib friction bumps around the edge, and **3 mic holes** over the Sense PDM mic.
- **Rule (CLAUDE.md): never edit the STLs — edit `pendant.py` and regenerate.** Run it from inside `3dprint/` (`python pendant.py --render` also produces `fit_preview.png`). Needs `pip install trimesh shapely manifold3d numpy`.
- The generator **auto-sizes the heart** to the smallest shape whose cavity holds the components — change a component constant and the whole case re-fits.

## Component layout (the decision, baked into the generator)

**Stacked, not side-by-side**: the LiPo lies flat and horizontal across the widest band of the heart; the XIAO sits **on top of it** on foam tape, component side toward the lid, **USB-C edge against the right wall** (1 mm from the slot). Stacking gives the smallest face (48.5 mm round heart); side-by-side would have needed a much larger one. Stack height 10.7 mm vs 11.0 mm usable cavity depth. The generator auto-picks the vertical band with the deepest fit margin for the battery.

**The header pins ("feet")**: they're breadboard headers, not fixings — nothing in the case uses them. **Clip them flush with side cutters** (the cavity assumes it): they'd otherwise add ~8 mm of depth and press into the battery pouch. Solder the three signal wires (touch → GPIO1, LED → GPIO2, plus 3V3/GND) into the through-holes from the top side — no desoldering needed. **The camera module unplugs** (lift the FPC latch); we only use the mic on the Sense board.

## Assembly

1. Battery in first, flat, wires exiting on the **left** side (dedicated slack space). The XIAO has no JST socket — cut the connector and solder the leads to the **BAT+/BAT− pads** under the board (mind polarity; the on-board circuit then charges via USB-C).
2. Foam tape on the battery, XIAO on top, USB-C aligned in the slot — test a cable before closing.
3. WS2812B (3V3/GND/DIN→GPIO2) taped inside, facing the lid. Copper-tape touch pad inside the lid face, wire to GPIO1.
4. Drop the lid into the rebate (pulse face out) — the edge bumps give the friction; pry it out at the tip notch. Chain through the bail.

## Print settings (42 fablab / LabElec)

**PETG or PLA** (material/finish decided later), 0.2 mm layers, 2–3 perimeters, infill ≥ 25 %. **Both parts print flat — body back-face down, lid plate down with the pulse relief up** — no supports needed anywhere (the USB slot roof self-bridges). ~1h30 total. Print one test lid first to check the drop-in fit (adjust `CLEAR` / `BUMP_R` in `pendant.py` if too tight/loose).
